findings.summary: Repair round 1 delivered ZERO DELTA and was re-issued REVISE by an independent audit that recomputed everything fresh: team branch tip af164b9 is the SAME git object already rejected under run 32864270667; no commit exists between accepted base 7669dcd and the team branch, so RF1–RF6 are unaddressed by construction. Auditor's independent recomputation this session: work-compression claims NOT MEASURED (still no R0_TRACES.jsonl/R0_RESULTS.json/journals/overlay; ledger+handoff still 0 bytes); test suite 10 failed / 17 passed (identical failure set); resolver RF1 crash reproduced live on all five multi-candidate cells E1/E2/E4/E7/E8; gold-keyed decoys still retrieve above τ=0.30 on E8 at coverage 1.333/1.000 ranked above every genuine capsule, RESOLVER_FP_GOLDKEYED still absent from analyze_r0.py, coverage normalization can exceed 1.0 (raw 1.5 recomputed); ALREADY_SATISFIED still unreachable by construction (P2-anchor before P3-not-authed + missing already_satisfied key in resolve() early-gap return, both probed directly); overhead accounting still fabricated (verify_ms += 0.05 hardcoded; reuse_yield dead code; maintenance overhead computed nowhere; baseline fallback arms get full default budgets while RT subtracts reused actions). What survives unchanged: D4 derivation layer honest and validated-for-current-test (12/12 capsules byte-identical, all CANDIDATE, credential lint holds); non-hermetic suite confirmed (running pytest regenerates committed registry/_derivation_report.json in place, which pins host-absolute /home/runner paths unreproducible from committed layout).

ROOT CAUSE of the second zero-delta resubmission (LOG-ONLY, this bundle is the sole witness): the OpenCode repair session never edited anything because it ABORTED at 17:06:03Z when the agent requested `external_directory` read access to `/home/runner/work/Spider/Sparkle/runtime/accounting.py` — a hallucinated path naming a NONEXISTENT project ('Sparkle' instead of 'Spider'); permission auto-rejection terminated the whole session (~2m47s in, after only reads: roles, directives, audit gate, resolver.py, loop.py, derivation.py, addressing.py, registry.py, tests). The agent had just stated it understood RF1/RF2 ('resolver.py:180 ch["capsule"] subscript on Segment'). Retry wrapper printed 'attempt 1/6' and NEVER retried (no attempt 2/6 anywhere in log). The workflow then ran its scope gate on a clean tree (passed trivially), found 'nothing to commit' at persist, and force-pushed the unchanged af164b9 as the round-1 team output with conclusion=success. This is instance #5 of the permission-auto-rejection session-killer family (CF-05/CF-13/CF-22 lineage: Graph #5, Product #1 builder, Product #3 architect wrong-path, Product #4 builder) and a NEW VARIANT: cross-project name contamination inside an absolute path rather than a config self-probe or canonicalization bug.

Workspace-copy ambiguity around delivery (unresolved mechanism question for the zero-delta failure family): during the TEAM agent session its own git status showed staged docs/roles/{GRAPH_RUNNER,PHYSICS_RUNNER}.md overlay edits pre-existing on runtime-repair-base (agent explicitly left them untouched as unrelated infra overlays); yet the workflow's persist step ~2m later saw 'nothing to commit, working tree clean', and the scope-enforce step passed with empty BAD. Mirror image in the AUDITOR job: its agent session's shell showed staged docs/roles edits at 17:23:45Z while its own enforce step (allowing only reports/audit/ + results/audit/) passed at 17:24:17Z. Consistent hypothesis (UNCONFIRMED): OpenCode sessions operate on a control-plane-staged working copy (launcher stages /tmp/spider_control; audit mounted separately at /tmp/spider_runtime_repair_audit; auditor sandbox /tmp/opencode/rt_audit_r1) synced back to $GITHUB_WORKSPACE on success — so a mid-session death delivers nothing and produces a silent byte-identical push. If true, delivery semantics are copy-based and every persist step needs an explicit sync/delta assertion. Mechanism not provable from this bundle alone.

The auditor pre-committed an escalation rule in THIS run's gate: if the next repair round again submits an unchanged tree, the honest gate becomes BLOCKED (external/orchestration decision), not a third fix-list copy. Cross-run verification (curator, from Git): round 2 (run 32877702179) resubmitted the byte-identical af164b9/tree 44cda5fd and the round-2 audit gate is indeed BLOCKED with delta_since_prior_audit_bytes=0, citing exactly this escalation rule. Net effect of repair rounds 1–2 combined: two full lane dispatches consumed, zero code changes, lane still at REVISE-state scaffolding until the later fresh-work cycle.

~21.5 min wall for the whole run (17:02:58→17:24:33Z): TEAM ~3m07s (agent session ~2m47s, entirely wasted on reads before the abort), AUDITOR ~18m10s including 25 'OpenCode/Ox network signature detected; watching for a 300s stall before aborting the call' warnings (all in the auditor job; slow model responses taxed wall clock, zero aborts/backoffs materialized), RETURN-TO-BUILDER ~5s. Combined with round 2, two consecutive repair dispatches produced zero deltas; a cheap zero-diff/delivery assertion before pushing team branches would have converted both into fast explicit failures.

failure_signatures: PERMISSION_KILL_WRONG_PROJECT_PATH: external_directory auto-reject on /home/runner/work/Spider/Sparkle/* (nonexistent sibling project name inside an agent-constructed absolute path) kills the entire OpenCode session; retry wrapper counts the attempt but does not retry this failure class (instance #5 of the family; new variant).

ZERO_DELTA_REPAIR_DELIVERY: persist step force-pushes HEAD even when `git commit` reports 'nothing to commit' — no delta/delivery assertion between agent phase and push, so a dead or edit-free session publishes a byte-identical 'team output' branch under conclusion=success (second consecutive occurrence in the Runtime repair chain after 32864270667→this run; cf. Intel r2 detached-HEAD variant CF-10).

UNFILLED_COMMIT_TEMPLATE_FIELDS (recurrence): pushed commit message would have been 'Runtime cycle  repair  attempt 1: team output' (double-space empty slots; visible as af164b9's subject) — the exact metadata signature prior audits flagged; cosmetic here (nothing changed anyway) but confounds provenance automation keyed on it.

WORKSPACE_COPY_AMBIGUITY: workflow steps and agent sessions observe different git index states (staged docs/roles overlays visible to agents, absent at enforce/persist time); unresolved whether delivery is copy-based/sync-back — see ANOMALY finding.
ESCALATION_ZERO_DELTA_TO_BLOCKED: pre-declared second-offense rule (REVISE→REVISE→BLOCKED) now armed and subsequently fired durably on cycle/runtime/32877702179/audit.
research_opportunities: Structural fix bundle for the whole silent-delivery family (joins CF-10 proposal): (a) fail persist unless tip != base AND working-tree diff vs mounted base is non-empty; (b) degrade external_directory denials to single-tool-call skips instead of session death; (c) make the retry wrapper actually retry after permission aborts; (d) canonicalize/validate any absolute path an agent is about to touch against the real workspace root; (e) settle the workspace-copy question (finding 3) because delivery assertions depend on which tree persist reads.

Runtime-lane substance (unchanged, owned by the lane): RF1–RF6 remain fully open; per the BLOCKED round-2 gate, an external/orchestration decision was required on whether the repair runner executes repairs at all — overtaken by events: the lane later delivered fresh work via run 32887030457 (see its record), making 'restart as fresh cycle after BLOCKED' the demonstrated recovery path worth codifying.

Cheap watchdog idea surfaced by the auditor's clean-room behavior: assert `git diff --quiet` against the audited base at audit START and record the tree hash in the gate header, so zero-delta rounds are detected in seconds instead of after full recomputation.
